title: Blood electrolytes (potassium, sodium, calcium)
what: This is a blood test from a vein. It shows the level of salts in your blood that your heart, muscles, and nerves need.
why: For weakness, cramps, skipped heartbeats, while taking water pills, after vomiting or diarrhea, or with kidney disease.
duration: the blood draw takes a few minutes; results usually come the next day
tell_doctor: What medicines you take, especially water pills and blood pressure pills
If you take potassium, calcium, or vitamin D
If you had vomiting or diarrhea in the last few days

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually fasting: no food for 8 to 12 hours. Plain water is fine. Check with the lab.

prepare.title: The day before
prepare.text: For 24 hours, no alcohol and no hard workouts. Best not to smoke in the morning.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor what you take. They will decide if anything should change.

steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow for a short time
Do not pump your fist hard. It can make potassium look higher
The skin is wiped with antiseptic
A quick prick, and blood fills a tube
The needle comes out, and a cotton pad is pressed on the spot
feel: A quick prick, like a pinch
Sometimes slight dizziness. Tell the nurse
after: Press the cotton pad for 3 to 5 minutes and keep your arm straight
You can eat right away and go back to your usual day
Results usually come in 1 day. The lab will tell you when

faq.q: Why can potassium come out too high?
faq.a: If the band was on too long or you squeezed your fist hard. Then the doctor will ask you to repeat the test.
Usually yes. The test is done in the morning before eating. Check with the lab.

reminders.text: Electrolyte test tomorrow. Do not eat after dinner. Plain water is fine.
